Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis Medical Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Ramirez, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis Medical Devices demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:
1. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year
2. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
3. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
4. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
5. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
6. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
7. Inventory management and working capital optimization

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Raj will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Lisa will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and full year.

Looking ahead to Q4 2024, we expect total revenue of $1.28 billion to $1.32 billion, representing organic growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year, or 10% to 12% on a constant currency basis. This builds on our Q3 results of $1.22 billion, which saw 8% organic growth, propelled by 15% expansion in Structural Heart, led by robust adoption of our next-generation TAVR valve, ApexFlow Pro. This platform is gaining share from incumbents like Edwards' Sapien and Medtronic's Evolut in the intermediate-risk cohort. By geography, U.S. revenue is set for 12% to 14% organic growth, driven by our Electrophysiology franchise, particularly the RhythmSync mapping system, where Q3 procedure volumes rose 18% as hospitals shifted to pulsed-field ablation from traditional RF methods. EMEA growth is guided at 6% to 8%, moderated by reimbursement delays in Germany for our neuromodulation leads, echoing challenges with Abbott's Infinity DBS system. APAC targets 15% to 17% organic growth, with China providing more than half via NMPA approval for our CardioPulse wearable ECG monitor and growing installed base of the RoboCath Xi robotic-assisted PCI platform in 25 key-tier hospitals. Emerging markets expect 10% growth from tenders in Brazil and India for peripheral vascular stents.

New launches will contribute tailwinds, including initial ramp from the FDA-cleared NeuroStim V2 burst-mode SCS device, offering 20% better paresthesia-free relief than Medtronic's Intellis for chronic pain, and our AI-enhanced OCT imaging catheter for coronary interventions, integrating with Philips' Azurion systems for real-time plaque characterization. For margins, Q4 adjusted gross margin is projected at 68.5% to 69.5%, up 150 basis points from Q3's 67.2%, thanks to efficiencies at our new Greenville, South Carolina facility offsetting 2% FX headwinds from a stronger USD versus EUR and JPY. Nitinol and bioabsorbable polymer costs have stabilized after 2023 disruptions, with $25 million in annualized savings from Value Engineering Program 2.0, redesigning 15 SKUs in endoscopy while upholding ISO 13485 standards. Adjusted operating margin guides to 24.0% to 25.0%, up 200 basis points YoY, with OpEx at 43.5% of revenue—R&D steady at 12% funding $150 million for the MIRASOL gene-editing platform in hemocompatibility coatings, and SG&A leverage from digital sales tools increasing rep productivity 22% in CRM procedures.

For full fiscal 2025, we're raising revenue guidance to $5.25 billion to $5.40 billion, implying 8% to 10% organic growth, surpassing industry consensus of 6-7% per Evaluate MedTech. This includes $200 million from new products like the global launch of OrthoFlex 3D-printed acetabular cups, matching Stryker's Triathlon kinematics but with 30% faster robotic integration. U.S. at 11% growth with TAVR share to 28%; EMEA 5% to 7% assuming DRG stability; APAC 14%+ as China exceeds $400 million via Local Manufacturing Exemptions; Rest of World 9%. FY25 gross margin 69.0% to 70.0% from 4% supply chain diversification away from Taiwan polymers and $50 million tariff mitigation through Mexico reshoring. Operating margin to 25.5% to 26.5%, EPS $5.85 to $6.05 at 20% tax rate post Irish IP restructuring. Our 'Precision Growth 2025' framework drives this: 60% incremental revenue from innovation including two H1 tuck-ins in digital therapeutics; 25% from 50 new J&J-partnered ASEAN deals; 15% from $300 million productivity savings fueling 14% R&D intensity. Risks like U.S. Medicare cuts or China stent procurement are buffered by 65% recurring revenue from services and sensors. We're poised for above-market growth and margin expansion in this $600 billion market.

Now, let's talk about procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Procedure volumes are the lifeblood of our business, powering unit growth and revenue in Cardiovascular, Orthopaedics, Endoscopy, and Neuromodulation. Q3 showed global volumes up 14% YoY for our technologies, accelerating from Q1's 11%, reaching 92% of pre-pandemic levels as elective procedures snap back. Cardiovascular, 42% of Q3 revenue, grew 16% YoY, with U.S. TAVR volumes up 18% on expanded indications and activations, pushing penetration to 25% of severe aortic stenosis cases—our next-gen valve gaining 5% share in low-risk. EP procedures rose 15% YoY with mapping systems like Biosense Webster's CARTO equivalents, OR utilization at 85% from 78%. Peripheral vascular moderated to 9% amid CMS APC cuts of 2.7%.

Orthopaedics, 28% of revenue, expanded 13% YoY, U.S. hip/knee up 15% to 98% of 2019 peaks with robotic systems akin to Stryker Mako or Zimmer ROSA; Triad cementless revisions saw double-digits on demographics and productivity. Europe lagged at 8% from NHS backlogs and German DRGs, offset by ASC ortho up 22% YoY to 18% U.S. mix. Endoscopy/Vision up 12% on GI screening at 75% pre-COVID per MGMA, single-use scopes competing Olympus EVIS X1. Neuromodulation surged 17%, SCS implants expanding share to 14% mimicking Nevro HF10.

U.S. led at 16% YoY (62% revenue), Europe 9% on staffing shortages (12% nurse vacancies per Deloitte), APAC 18% with China 22% post-zero-COVID via JV robotics, Japan 12% on SCS reimbursements, emerging 20% on low-cost tech. Industry-wide, 1.2 billion H1 procedures up 13% per IQVIA/Definuisse, electives at 95% 2019 levels. ASPs grew 2-3%, our premium mix 4%. Tailwinds: AI procedure planning boosting adoption 25%, connected OR at 40% cases; new EP catheter for 15% efficiency, ASC TAVR labeling ($500M TAM), MR-compatible SCS lead. Partnerships with Epic/Cerner cut times 12%. Q4 volumes 13-15% YoY, risks CMS cuts 3.5% or semiconductor volatility, but $2.5B R&D (18% revenue) positions us.

Moving on to organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Excluding our NeuroStim Solutions acquisition and FX, Q3 organic growth was 8.7%, full-year to date 9.2%, beating medtech's 6% average like Medtronic/Boston Scientific, on volumes, share gains, and pipeline amid demographics and recovery.

Cardiovascular (42% revenue): +12.5% Q3/+13.8% YTD, VitalFlow Ultra TAVR at 15% U.S. share post-FDA PMA, 18% volumes vs. 12% industry (DAR 360); interventional +11% on Xcelerate sirolimus stents (25% lower restenosis per PROVE-IT); peripheral +9% atherectomy; margins +220bps to 68% via Galway efficiencies.

Orthopedics & Spine (28%): +7.2% Q3/+8.1% YTD, despite ASC labor; cementless knees +10% Triad obese indications; spine +14% Concerto cages in 40% robotic (vs. Medtronic Inspire), +2pts share in $5.5B U.S. via 18% readmission bundles; mid-teens FY25 on AI planning.

Advanced Surgical (20%): +6.8% Q3/+7.5% YTD, VisioClear scopes +9% infection control; VitalRobotics +22% to 450 systems, utilization 28 cases/week, 75% recurring.

Diabetes & Monitoring (10%): +4.9% Q3/+5.6% YTD, VitalSense CGM EU MDR ramp, pump attach 42%, CLARITY-2 1.2% HbA1c drop.

Geography: U.S. (62%) +10.2% Q3/+11.1% YTD on 7% procedures, CY2024 MPFS; EMEA (22%) +6.4%/+6.9% despite DRGs, Galway +20k sq ft; APAC (12%) +8.9%/+9.7%, China +15% NMPA; RoW (4%) +5.1%/+5.8%, LATAM +11%.

Our 'Innovate, Penetrate, Expand' drove 12 launches, 9.5% R&D (3.2x NPV), NeuroStim M&A; TAVR CAGR 15% to 2028, GLP-1 ortho tailwinds; FY25 guide 9-11%, cardio/robotics lead.

Next, impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

These drove Q3's 8% organic growth, +220bps gross to 67.5%, EBITDA 28.2%—five-quarter high. Pricing yielded +3.2% ASPs via mix (EvoStent/NeuroPulse +15% share, 12-15% premiums). U.S. (55% revenue) +2.8% despite 1.5% IPPS cut, Outcomes360 evidence (25% readmissions drop vs. Synergy), NTAP extensions $45M. Europe (25%) +1.9%, FlexiTitan +8% EUPROMAC/sustainability (30% recycled Ti); emerging (20%) +4.5% tiered. Pricing +1.5pts growth, mix +1pt; 2024 low-single ASPs via digital twins (20% time cuts).

Costs: $180M run-rate savings (4.2% COGS). Supply: 40% Mexico localization, -18% logistics, Ti stable post-Ukraine. Manufacturing: Six Sigma 15% yields, $120M CapEx automation -22% labor, Galway 98% OEE. R&D: cut 12 projects, 11.2% sales. SG&A: +2% headcount, AI +14% productivity. APAC $50M, U.S. GPO 9%. 'MedTech 2025' bundles +30% stickiness; FY gross 67-68%.

Then, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

Post-Q3 18% growth to $1.2B, +150bps EBITDA to 32%, Q4 executes 'Innovate, Expand, Optimize' for $600B market (5.8% CAGR).

Pillar 1 Innovation (40% CapEx): EchoArm 2.0 haptic/AI robotics FDA IDE, 25 U.S. sites, $25-30M rev, 28% time cut vs. Hugo; NeuroPulse AI CE/submission, 800-trial patients 85% relief; OrthoPredict IoT to 200 hospitals, Epic integration $50M SaaS. 12-15% ROI.

Pillar 2 Expansion: U.S. 65% robust CY2025 OPPS; Europe 20% Watchman FLX Pro 35% gains, 1,200 implants; APAC 25% China EchoArm NMPA/$2B TAM, Shanghai 40% local; emerging 30% consumables; structural heart 22%, ophtho VisioGuide.

Pillar 3 Resilience: dual-source 90% nitinol, $100M WC release; SG&A -300bps AI; Galway 68% gross; ESG Scope1 -20%; $500M M&A dry powder. Q4 $1.28-1.32B (17-20%), EPS $1.85-1.95, 15% core.

Key assumptions underlying the guidance.

For FY25 8-10% organic ($4.85-4.95B const FX), gross 66.5-67.5% (+100-150bps), op 24.5-25.5%, EPS $5.45-5.65 (repurchase/tax 18.5%). Procedures: U.S. 5-7%, cardio 6-8% TAVR (NeoFlow 12% share), neuro 4-6% Percept; EMEA 6-8% ortho, APAC 12-15% China NMPA/stents, Japan 7%. Pricing -1.5-2.5% ASP (OPPS flat, value contracts +3%, emerging -2%). Costs: Galway 200bps eff, +3-4% materials hedged, $15M FX tail, disposables 65%. Pipeline: $250M Hugo RAS/digital CloudMed. M&A neutral-$50M, OpEx +7%, 70/30 recurring. Balanced: demographics/innovation vs. pricing/costs.

Finally, inventory management and working capital optimization.

Q3 DIO 58 days (-17% YoY), turns 6.3x (>5.1x median), CCC 42 days (DSO 51, DPO 71), $145M freed (12% TTM rev), WC 14.2% (<16.8% index). Funds $220M R&D robotics ($8B TAM).

SAP/Palantir AI 92% forecast, VMI high-velocity -28% stock 99.5% service; RFID/ABC: JIT A-items neurostim, consignment B ortho, outsource C. U.S. consignment -25 DIO ASC/EP; Europe HTA/Dublin; China Suzhou 45 days; LATAM blockchain. Dual-source 20% cut, IoT smart expiry -12% waste. Year-end DIO 55, supports 8-10% growth/28% EBITDA.

I will now turn the call over to Michael for a review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. As highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter. Q3 revenue hit $1.22 billion, up 8% organically, with gross margins at 67.2% and operating margins advancing on cost discipline. Expenses were controlled, R&D at 12% of revenue supporting our pipeline, SG&A leveraged through productivity gains. Profitability strengthened, adjusted EPS reflecting these trends. For guidance, as Dr. Vasquez detailed, Q4 revenue $1.28-1.32 billion and FY25 raised to $5.25-5.40 billion, with margin expansion from efficiencies and mix.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of EchoArm 2.0 robotic platform is progressing well, and we anticipate it will revolutionize structural heart and soft-tissue procedures with haptic feedback and AI tissue differentiation, reducing times 28% versus competitors. R&D efforts include NeuroPulse AI closed-loop SCS with 85% efficacy, OrthoPredict IoT analytics, and MIRASOL coatings, backed by $2.5 billion pipeline and 18% revenue investment for 12 IDEs and bioresorbables.

Next, Lisa with insights on our commercial strategy.

Lisa Ramirez:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Our commercial team has driven product adoption. We're expanding market presence in APAC via China localization and NMPA wins, EMEA tenders for TAVR/LAA, and U.S. ASCs/IDNs with value bundles. Customer engagement enhanced through digital tools boosting productivity 22%, partnerships like J&J in ASEAN, and 50 new deals targeting 25% international growth.

Now, back to Dr. Vasquez for Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks. On procedure volumes, how sustainable is the 14% growth given labor constraints?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, John. Sustainability comes from our tech leadership—AI planning and connected OR boosting throughput 25%, Epic integrations cutting times 12%. U.S. at 16% with OR at 85%, APAC 18% on robotics JVs. Risks like CMS cuts are offset by value-based models; we see 13-15% in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Regarding FY25 guidance raise, what gives confidence amid FX and China risks?

Michael Chen:
Emily, confidence stems from $200M new product ramps like OrthoFlex and NeuroStim V2, 60% innovation in Precision Growth. Recurring 65% buffers China procurement; supply diversification and $300M savings fuel margins to 26.5%. Assumptions hold with procedures mid-single and APAC 14%+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you elaborate on commercial expansion in emerging markets?

Lisa Ramirez:
Absolutely, David. Q4 priorities include 30% consumables ramp in India/Brazil with $800 EP catheters at 55% margins, tenders for stents, and distributor growth penetrating private networks 30% deeper. Affordable tech and vertical integration drive 10% emerging growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
On inventory optimization, any updates on smart inventory pilots?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Rachel, pilots with IoT in consignment cabinets forecast biologics expiry, cutting waste 12%. RFID and Palantir AI hit 92% accuracy, DIO to 55 by year-end. De-risked dual-sourcing supports growth without service disruptions.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
